name: opaline
description: Team-wide insight into your coding agents: where they waste time and money, and which mistakes keep coming back.

interface.shortDescription: Improve your team's coding agent setup
interface.longDescription:
Opaline helps your team improve its coding agent setup. It finds where agents get stuck or waste time and money across every teammate's sessions, so you can fix the instructions, docs, scripts and CI behind it.

Ask in plain words: "Where did our agents get stuck or waste the most time this month?", "Which repositories cost us the most, and why?", "What mistakes keep coming back in our agent runs?". Opaline looks through the sessions your team has uploaded, finds the patterns, reads the runs that show them and answers with the evidence and a suggested fix. A dashboard shows cost and usage by repository and model, and per member to see where each person's setup needs help.

Answers are saved, so the next question on the same topic updates the last answer instead of starting over, and you can share them with your workspace.

To start, each teammate connects their coding agents at opaline.so. After you install the plugin, it walks you through it.

Opaline only reads workspaces you belong to and never changes or deletes sessions.
capabilities: Find where your team's coding agents get stuck or waste time and money
Spot mistakes that keep coming back, and see whether a fix worked
Get a concrete fix for your setup: instructions, docs, scripts or CI
Save answers, update them later and share them with your workspace
defaultPrompt: Where did our coding agents get stuck or waste the most time this month?
Which repositories cost us the most over the last 4 weeks, and why?
What mistakes keep coming back in our agent runs?

positive.description: Where agents get stuck over a month
positive.prompt: Where did our coding agents get stuck or waste the most time over the last 30 days?
positive.expected_behavior: find, read and save_analysis may ask for permission once; choosing "always allow" is fine. States the scope it used (the last 30 days, every session the account can see) and the coverage from the find header. Names a few concrete causes, such as agents following outdated web-app docs and repeated no-console lint failures, ranked by time and cost, each backed by runs it read from more than one member, and says how many runs it read out of how many matched. Suggests a setup fix for each (docs, scripts, lint config or instructions), saves the answer and then gives it in full.

positive.prompt: Which repositories cost our team the most over the last 4 weeks, and why?
positive.expected_behavior: find, read and save_analysis may ask for permission once; choosing "always allow" is fine. Gives the estimated API cost in USD per repository for the stated date range, mentions any unpriced runs, and explains what drove the cost in the top repositories from runs it read (for example repeated retries in web-app), with a setup fix where one applies. Does not rank people. Saves the answer and then gives it in full.

positive.prompt: What mistakes keep coming back in our agent runs over the last 6 weeks?
positive.expected_behavior: find, read and save_analysis may ask for permission once; choosing "always allow" is fine. Groups failed tool calls by cause, reads a sample of the runs behind the largest groups and names the recurring mistakes with run evidence from several weeks and members: agents following outdated web-app docs (a missing typecheck script, dollars instead of cents) and repeated no-console lint failures. Suggests a setup fix for each (for example update the docs, or add the lint rule to the agent instructions), does not rank people, and saves the answer before giving it.

positive.prompt: Show the Opaline dashboard for our team for the last 30 days.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the Opaline dashboard in the chat for the last 30 days, with estimated API cost, sessions and agent runs over time and breakdowns by repository and model. It does not answer with a link instead and needs no permission prompt.

positive.description: Update an earlier answer and share it
positive.prompt: Check again where our agents get stuck, update the earlier answer if there is one, and share it with my workspace.
positive.expected_behavior: find, read and save_analysis may ask for permission once; choosing "always allow" is fine. Searches the saved answers first. If one on the same topic exists (for example from an earlier test), it says so, looks only at sessions after the last day that answer covered, saves a new answer that says which findings were confirmed, weakened, new or dropped, and says it updated the earlier answer; otherwise it answers from scratch. Then shares the saved answer with the workspace and confirms it is shared.

negative.description: Deleting sessions is not supported: no tool deletes or edits session data
negative.prompt: Delete all of my coding sessions from last week in Opaline.

negative.description: Billing changes are not supported: the plugin cannot change plans or take payments
negative.prompt: Upgrade my Opaline workspace to the paid plan.

negative.description: Workspaces the account does not belong to are not accessible
negative.prompt: Show the coding agent costs of the acme-corp workspace in Opaline.

review.commerce_description: Opaline does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT or Codex.

publication.release_notes: Opaline now focuses on improving your team's agent setup: find where agents get stuck or waste time, and what to fix. The assistant uses six tools with plain descriptions; the dashboard's data tools are used only by the dashboard. Answers follow one cycle: find a saved answer, look only at what happened since, and save the update as a new answer that says how each finding changed. find and read keep their calls as a private draft that nobody can open; it is kept only when save_analysis saves it, and unsaved drafts are deleted after 7 days. A saved answer is never changed.
